content_warning.description: The content warning each Note is shown behind.

edits.description:

id.description: The route's stable id, part of every announcement's key.

language.description: The language each Note is written in, as an ISO 639 code.

late_release.description:

the tag's post to it, or posts it anew where the destination cannot
edit (`edit`); posts it anew (`post`); or leaves the tag's post
(`skip`).

living.description:
Whether it keeps one post of each report it takes, edited each
window where the destination edits and posted anew each window
where it cannot; it names only reports among its sources.

match.description:
What of an event it narrows its sources' events by, an event taken
only where every key holds; every event its other keys take where
absent.

pin.description:
Whether to pin each announcement in place of the route's earlier pin,
and how the earlier pin is found: `true` finds it by its marker, as
"markers" does, and `false` pins nothing. A living route pins its
post where absent and the destination pins.

private.description:
Whether its place is private, so it may take a private or internal
repository's events; a place is public where absent, and a config
sending such events to it does not load (`[doctor] private_to_public`).
A route taking a private kind, such as `alert`, says it either way:
`false` sends them to a public place on purpose (`[doctor]
private_kinds`).

thread.description: The thread to open for each announcement.

silence.description:

url.description:

what a webhook herald registers points at. A setup command's `--url`
takes its place.

work.description: How the work a request leaves keeps within its host's limits.

Sessions.description:
`[server.sessions]`: how a session a destination holds waits before it
connects again, each wait double the last up to the longest, and how old
a command one taken up again answers.

first_wait.description: The first wait after a session fails to connect; "1s" where absent.

jitter.description:
Whether each wait is between half of it and all of it, so sessions
that failed together do not all connect again at once; true where
absent.

longest_wait.description:
The longest wait between attempts; "1m" where absent, and at least
`first_wait`.

stale.description:
How long ago a command a session taken up again answers may have
been given; one given earlier is skipped and logged; "10m" where
absent.

Severity.description: How severe an alert is, in lowercase on every forge.

oneOf.description: Critical.
High.
Medium, GitHub's `moderate` for a Dependabot alert.
Low.
GitLab's informational.
GitLab's unknown.

A code scanning rule's error, where its alert has no security
severity.
A code scanning rule's warning.
A code scanning rule's note.

SharedList.description:
A shared block list, as `lists` writes it: a file of domains to block in
the CSV form Mastodon exports, pinned by the SHA-256 of its text.

file.description: The file, as a path beside `herald.toml`.

sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the file's text, in hex: a list that changes is not
read until its new digest is pinned.

Signal.description: What a source announces of a repository.

oneOf.description: A published Release.
A version tag, with or without a Release.

A version of a package the forge's registry holds for the
repository.

commit status where the source reads checks.

scanning's, or a GitLab vulnerability.

review, merged or closed.

Size.description: A number of bytes: a number and KiB or MiB, as "1MiB".

SlackInteractions.description: How a Slack destination takes commands.

app.description:
The secret holding an app-level token (`xapp-…`) with
`connections:write`, which opens Socket Mode connections.

command.description:
The slash command members give, followed by a command and a project:
`/herald latest php-mutation-gate`.

domains.description:
Domains beside its Slack's own a Socket Mode session may connect
under, such as a proxy's.

name.description:
The name its app and bot user go by in the manifest `herald setup`
prints: up to 35 lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `-` or `_`, and
`herald` where unset.

prereleases.description:
Whether `latest` and `changelog` answer with a pre-release newer than
every release.

replies.description: Who sees the answers to `latest` and `changelog`.

signing.description:
The secret holding the app's signing secret, which each request
posted to herald is checked against.

template.description:
The template `latest` takes its title from and `changelog` its body,
in place of the route's own.

wording.description:
What it says back and how it describes its commands, phrase by
phrase, each a template over `project`, `projects`, `named` and
`command`; herald's own words for every phrase left out.

SlackRoute.description: A route to a Slack destination.

channel.description:
The channel's id, such as `C0123456789`, which the bot has joined. A
bot needs one; a webhook posts where it was made.

edits.description:
Which changed announcements it edits the post of: none, or a Release
whose name or notes the forge says were edited (`release`).

group.description:
How it gathers the events that share a key into one announcement;
each event is announced alone where absent.

id.description: The route's stable id, part of every announcement's key.

kinds.description: The kinds of event it takes; every kind where absent.

late_release.description:
What it does with a Release whose tag it already announced: edits
the tag's post to it, or posts it anew where the destination cannot
edit (`edit`); posts it anew (`post`); or leaves the tag's post
(`skip`).

living.description:
Whether it keeps one post of each report it takes, edited each
window where the destination edits and posted anew each window
where it cannot; it names only reports among its sources.

match.description:
What of an event it narrows its sources' events by, an event taken
only where every key holds; every event its other keys take where
absent.

pin.description:
Whether to pin each announcement in place of the route's earlier pin,
and how the earlier pin is found: `true` finds it by its marker, as
"markers" does, and `false` pins nothing. A living route pins its
post where absent and the destination pins.

private.description:
Whether its place is private, so it may take a private or internal
repository's events; a place is public where absent, and a config
sending such events to it does not load (`[doctor] private_to_public`).
A route taking a private kind, such as `alert`, says it either way:
`false` sends them to a public place on purpose (`[doctor]
private_kinds`).

sources.description: The sources it takes events from.

subscribe.description: How the route offers subscribing, where it mentions its subscribers.

template.description:
The template it renders with; none on a route to a herald feed or
push, which carries each event as an envelope.

thread.description: The thread to open for each announcement.

versions.description:
The versions it takes, as a pattern in which `*` stands for any run
of characters and `?` for any one, such as `"*.*.*"`, which leaves
out a Docker Hub tag such as `latest`; every version where absent.

withdraw.description:
What it does with an announcement whose Release the forge deletes:
keeps its post (`keep`), or deletes every message herald recorded of
it where the destination can (`delete`).

SlackSubscribe.description:
What a route says about subscribing on Slack, where it mentions its
subscribers.

button.description:
Whether each announcement carries a button that subscribes, or
unsubscribes a member already subscribed.

SlackVia.description: How Slack carries commands to herald.

oneOf.description:
Slack posts each command and button press to herald's endpoint,
signed with the app's signing secret: served by `herald server` and
by a serverless driver.

herald holds a Socket Mode connection, opened with the app-level
token, and takes each one from it: served by `herald server` and by a
Cloudflare Worker's Durable Object, with no public endpoint.
A GitHub repository's releases, tags and packages.

api.description:
The API's base URL, for a forge that is not GitHub, GitLab.com or
Codeberg: a GitHub Enterprise Server's `https://ghe.example/api/v3`,
a GHE.com tenant's `https://api.acme.ghe.com`, a self-managed or
Dedicated GitLab's `https://gitlab.example/api/v4`, or a Forgejo's
`https://forge.example/api/v1`. Where absent, it is the CI run's own
when announcing the run's repository, and otherwise the forge's
public instance. An owner is listed at the same base.

app.description:
The GitHub App the source reads as, by the name of its
`[github_apps.<name>]` table, in place of `token`: herald mints an
installation token for each round.

backfill.description:
How many of the newest releases, tags and package versions the first
poll announces;
none where absent (ADR-0003). For an owner, it applies to the members
the first listing finds; a member found later announces only what it
publishes after it was found.

discovery.description:
How an owner source finds the repositories that join or leave it:
listing the owner each round ("list"), or only where it holds no
listing, its selection changed or a delivery said the owner's
repositories changed ("push"); "list" where absent.

edits_depth.description:
How many of the newest Releases a poll watches for an edit of their
name or notes, where a route taking the source edits them
(`edits = "release"`); 30 where absent, and at most `page`.

exclude.description:
The names left out, as `include` writes them, whatever `include`
says.

feed_page.description:
How many activities one page of a Forgejo owner's feed asks for
under `transport = "feed"`; 50 where absent, and at most 200.

feed_pages.description:
How many pages of a Forgejo owner's feed a round reads back before
it polls every member; 3 where absent, and at most 12.

graphql.description:
The GraphQL endpoint of a GitHub or GitLab owner source; beside
`api` where absent: `/api/graphql` on a GitHub Enterprise Server
whose `api` ends in `/api/v3` and on GitLab, whose `api` ends in
`/api/v4`, and `/graphql` on GitHub and GHE.com.

graphql_batch.description:
How many members one GraphQL request asks for; 50 where absent, and
at most 100.

include.description:
The names of the owner's repositories taken, as globs in which `*`
stands for any run of characters, `?` for any one and `[...]` for
any one of a class, ignoring case; every name where absent.

installation.description:
The id of the App's installation tokens are minted for; looked up
on the owner, or on the repository, where absent.

issues.description:
Which issues are announced where the signals take "issue": what
they did, and their labels and authors; every issue opened, closed
or reopened where absent.

keep_members.description:
How long a member that left the selection keeps its cursor before it
is forgotten; "30d" where absent.

key.description:
The field each entry of the member file names its repository by;
"name" where absent.

language.description:
Languages, any one of which a member is written in; any where
absent.

listed_page.description:
How many repositories one page of the listing asks for; 100 where
absent on GitHub and GitLab, and 50 on Forgejo, whose instances
answer at most 50 unless configured otherwise.

member_hooks.description:
Who registers a project webhook on each member of a GitLab owner,
whose group cannot send its own on GitLab Free: no one ("off"),
`herald hooks <name>` ("setup"), or each poll round too ("round");
"off" where absent. Each hook points at `[server] url` and is signed
with `webhook`.

members.description:
The member file: where given, the names it lists are the source's
members, which the filters narrow, read as TOML or JSON by its
extension.

most_listed.description:
The most repositories a listing reads before the filters; 10000
where absent. A listing over it refuses the source for the round.

most_members.description:
The most members the filters may keep; 1000 where absent, and at
most 100000. A selection over it refuses the source for the round.

most_packages.description:
The most entries one listing of packages reads; 1000 where absent,
and at most 100000. A listing over it refuses the source for the
round.

moving.description:
The container tags that move from one image to the next, which are
never announced, as globs as `include` writes them; `["latest"]`
where absent.

owner.description:
The organization, GitLab group or user whose repositories are the
source's members, each polled on its own, in place of `repository`.

package_types.description:
The types of package announced where the signals take "package", as
the forge names them, such as `["container", "npm"]`; every type
where absent. GitHub's are npm, maven, rubygems, docker, nuget and
container.

package_visibility.description:
Who may see a package's version: the stricter of the package's own
visibility and its repository's ("stricter"), or the package's own
("package"); "stricter" where absent. A version not everyone may see
reaches only `private` routes under `[doctor] private_to_public =
"refuse"`.

packages.description:
The packages announced, as globs as `include` writes them; every
package where absent.

page.description:
How many of the newest releases, and of the newest tags, one poll
reads; 30 where absent.

parse.description:
The most of an answer parsed; "4MiB" where absent, and at most four
times that.

prefer.description:
Which of a tag and its Release is announced where a repository's
signals take both: the Release, a tag with none waiting for it as
long as `tag_window` ("release"), or whichever comes first
("first"); "release" where absent. Holding a tag needs a store that
keeps held events, which the markers store does not.

prerelease.description:
How a pre-release is told: by the forge's flag or a pre-release part
in the version ("either"), by the flag alone ("flag"), or by the
version alone ("tag"); "either" where absent. A tag carries no flag,
and neither does a GitLab release.

project.description:
The project a member's events are announced as, a template of
`repository.name`, `repository.path`, `repository.owner`,
`repository.id`, `repository.topics`, `repository.properties` and
`repository.visibility`; the repository's name where absent.

properties.description:
Custom properties, every one of which a member holds with one of the
values given, such as `{ team = "media", tier = ["core", "edge"] }`.

pulls.description:
Which pull requests are announced where the signals take
"pull-request": what they did, whether drafts are, and their labels
and authors; every pull request opened, ready for review or merged
where absent.

registry.description:
The host of the container registry an image is named on, as in
`registry.example:5000`: where absent, ghcr.io beside GitHub's API,
`containers.<host>` beside a GitHub Enterprise Server's or a GHE.com
tenant's, each image's own on GitLab, and the instance's on Forgejo.

remembered.description:
How many identities the cursor remembers, newest first; 500 where
absent, and at least `page`.

repositories.description:
What the source makes of the repositories each glob names, as
`include` writes them; where several name one repository, the
narrowest that sets a key gives it.

repository.description:
The repository, as `owner/name`, or a GitLab project's full path,
such as `group/subgroup/name`; or `owner` in its place.

runs.description:
Which runs are announced where the signals take "run": what they
are read from, what they did, how they ended, and their branches,
triggers and workflows; every finished run of the forge's own CI
where absent.

signals.description:
What the source announces of each repository: its published Releases,
its version tags, the versions of its packages, or several;
`["release"]` where absent. A tag and a Release of it share one
identity, so each route announces it once.

subgroups.description:
Whether a GitLab group's members include the projects of its
subgroups; true where absent.

tables.description:
The arrays of the member file that list repositories, such as
`["repo", "ungoverned"]`; the file's own array where absent, which
only JSON can hold.

tag_window.description:
How long a tag with no Release waits for one, counted from when
herald first sees the tag; "1h" where absent, and at most "7d".

template.description: Whether template repositories are taken.

token.description:
A token that reaches a private repository or raises the API's rate
limit, such as the run's `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

topics.description: Topics, any one of which a member holds; any where absent.

visibility.description:
The visibilities taken; only public repositories where absent. A
repository whose visibility the forge does not name is private. A
route that takes a private or internal member is refused unless it
is `private` (`[doctor] private_to_public`).

webhook.description:
The secret the forge signs its webhook deliveries to `herald server`
with: GitHub's and Forgejo's webhook secret, or GitLab's signing
token (ADR-0007). An owner source takes its repositories' and its
organization's deliveries, and announces one only where the owner's
last membership record holds the repository when its work runs.
